title: candid or plandid scene in taxi driver (1976)

commenti.body:
I have no incite but I lived in a big city and that stuff happens ALL the time. I just watched taxi driver for the first time the other week and that scene stood out as unique. I think there is a healthy amount of symbolism with it too.

I think that happens when Travis is following the two girls on the side walk. They don’t bat and eye at the crazy guy but are more concerned and scared of Travis, then the older one says to just ignore him.

I know the scene and I have always thought it was probably just a legit slice of life filming that he picked up and used. A lot of directors in the 70s just filmed all the time and I think he just used this in the final cut.

It was indeed a very realistic scene, specially if you live in big cities, but this man was an actor named Frank Adu (RIP), he was credited as "angry black man", and if i remember correctly, this scene was also in the script. 

https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075314/characters/nm0012524

Scorsese mentioned on the commentary with pride that though that man is an actor, all the people watching this freak out aren’t extras and are just there.
